Synopsis:
An overworked coffin maker. He's gruff and unfriendly. In this dialogue, if you've spoken to the bereaved couple, you can try to convince him to make a coffin for a child.

Cluster Contexts:
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_CoffinMaker.json: Ulkov Sully is an overworked, gruff coffin maker who’s bluntly uninterested in other people’s tragedies and keeps a strict backlog — his default is to refuse new work. His shop is fully booked and he’ll only bump someone in the queue for a price, so conversations may trigger a check for gold or a demand for payment. If you’ve already talked to the bereaved couple and pressed the issue, you can try to persuade him to make a coffin for a child (appeals to sympathy or paying to jump the queue are the obvious routes). The sample lines show his repeated refusals, apathetic shrugging, and the payment check; the other listed cluster scenes (Bhaal/temple content, etc.) don’t directly alter this local exchange.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_BereavedFather.json: A father that recently lost his child and has come to the graveyard with his wife to get a specially made coffin. In one set, the coffin maker has refused to make it as he's too busy - father is very upset. In the other set he's extremely thankful to the player for organising the coffin for his daughter.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_BereavedCouple.json: The bereaved father and mother are heartbroken and grieving. Their little girl was murdered and they can't get her a coffin - the coffin maker is too backed up.
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_Gravekeeper.json: A weary gravekeeper, absolutely exhausted at having to bury so many bodies in recent days. Would be good to have her have typical gallows humour, but be relatively kindhearted and helpful underneath it (though relatively unimportant) She will exclusively hang around the gravekeeper's house, and likely either be found sat and resting or just idly milling around a small area.Important topics:- Where you can find a shovel- Killings in Baldur's Gate (with a branch for if it's solved)- (When you've encountered them) Kobold Looters- Something to chastise the player if they've gone around digging up graves themselves, probably a HasMet alt?
- LOW_KurwinCoffin_KoboldLooter.json: Auto-started when the party smashes/pries open a coffin, this scene finds a tetchy kobold — Bugthimble — caught looting the contents. She’s been tunnelling into the grave to pinch trinkets and stashed a haul inside, wears a face‑covering helmet, and is defensive and suspicious of outsiders. The players either dug here because a Courier note (found by Scratch) promised “enough valuables to settle matters between us,” or simply for sport, so they expect the chest’s contents or ownership. Bugthimble immediately claims she found the goods first but recognizes the name Nine‑Fingers and backs down or bargains when that name is invoked; the exchange can therefore turn to threats, bribes, or handing the crate over.
